candidates.name: Jeff Merkley
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2009 and former Speaker of the Oregon House; grew up in Portland, the son of a millworker. Known for leading filibuster-reform fights, including a record 22-plus-hour floor speech in 2025. Won the May 19 Democratic primary with 93.2% and is seeking a fourth term.

cost.label: Would 'end the gouging of Americans on drug prices by banning drug companies from charging more'; housing and child care 'should be affordable in every community' (campaign site)

health.label: 'Give every American the opportunity to participate in simple, seamless, cost-effective Medicare for All' (campaign site)

housing.label: End Hedge Fund Control of American Homes Act would force hedge funds to sell off single-family homes; backed mortgage relief for underwater homeowners (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Called family separation the 'dehumanization' of asylum seekers after his viral 2018 visit to a Texas detention site; co-sponsored the Dreamer Confidentiality Act protecting DACA recipients (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Attacks 'a rigged economy and tax system that continuously puts more and more money in the hands of those who already have the most' (campaign site)

climate.label: 'We must invest in a shift to 100% clean and renewable energy sources'; backs a Green New Deal (campaign site)

education.label: Reduce elementary class sizes, bring back shop classes, and let every young person 'go to college debt-free' (campaign site)

safety.label: Voted for the First Step Act expanding job training and early release and cutting mandatory minimums for nonviolent drug offenses (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Has 'fought to protect a woman's constitutional right to the full scope of comprehensive reproductive health care, including abortion'; co-sponsors a nationwide access guarantee (Senate office)

democracy.label: Backs required early voting periods, vote-by-mail, same-day registration, an end to gerrymandering, and overturning Citizens United (campaign site)

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 Senate election in Oregon (primary results)

candidates.name: David Brock Smith
candidates.background: Oregon state senator for coastal District 1 since 2023, previously in the state House (2017-2023) and on the Curry County Board of Commissioners; third-generation southwest Oregon resident from Port Orford who ran his family's restaurant. Won the May 19 Republican primary with 29.5% in a multi-candidate field.

taxes.label: 'No new taxes, more support for our local businesses, eliminating fraud, and reducing unnecessary government spending' (campaign issues page)

immigration.label: Signed a legislators' letter backing Gov. Greg Abbott's position in the Eagle Pass border standoff with federal authorities (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Has claimed human actions do not contribute to climate change, contradicting scientific consensus (Oregon Capital Chronicle)

safety.label: Campaign pledge to 'restore safety to our streets' and address addiction and homelessness 'with accountability' (Oregon Capital Chronicle)

democracy.label: Sponsored a 2025 bill to let voters repeal Oregon's vote-by-mail law; signed the 2020 letter urging Oregon's AG to back Texas's lawsuit contesting the presidential results (Oregon Capital Chronicle)

housing.label: Touted bills easing rural home siting and letting ADUs hook into existing sewer systems to get more homes built, HB 3442 and SB 835 (official 2023 session recap)

education.label: Co-authored SB 1100 giving tax credits for private school and homeschool costs plus parental notification and curriculum transparency mandates (The News Guard)

repro.label: 'A consistent vote for unborn children' who 'voted for numerous life-affirming bills' in the legislature (Oregon Right to Life PAC endorsement)

candidates.name: Tina Kotek
candidates.background: Governor since 2023 and the longest-serving House Speaker in Oregon history (2013-2022). Declared a homelessness state of emergency on her first day and set a goal of 36,000 new homes a year. Won the May 19 Democratic primary with 84% and is seeking a second term.
priorities: Reduce homelessness and build more housing
Improve schools and expand mental health and addiction care

cost.label: Touts canceling freeway tolls, reining in utility rate hikes, banning hidden junk fees, and shielding credit scores from medical debt (campaign announcement)

health.label: Signed SB 1089 (2023) creating the Universal Health Plan Governance Board to design 'a detailed, publicly funded, single-payer universal health plan' for Oregon (Healthcare Innovation)

housing.label: Mixed record: led HB 2001 abolishing single-family-only zoning statewide, while also signing $376M in affordable housing and shelter funding and creating a statewide shelter program (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Signed a 2026 package limiting ICE in Oregon: bans masked arrests, requires schools to alert parents when ICE appears, bars hospitals from sharing immigration status, and lets people sue federal agents over warrantless home entry (OPB)

taxes.label: Proposed withholding $1B of Oregon's kicker income tax rebate, aimed at 'high income earners', to fund wildfire prevention and suppression: 'We need to find some resources to do that' (OPB)

climate.label: Signed the 2023 Climate Resilience Package (HB 3409 and HB 3630) funding heat pump deployment, updated building codes and performance standards, EV rebates, and solar and storage programs (Environment America)

education.label: Invested in early literacy and summer learning and committed $50 million to expand affordable childcare (campaign announcement)

safety.label: Signed HB 4002 recriminalizing drug possession as 'a package that encourages treatment first, while balancing the need for accountability' (KGW)

repro.label: Campaigns on having protected abortion access and provider safety; co-founded the West Coast Health Alliance (campaign announcement)

democracy.label: Restarted Oregon's automatic Motor Voter registration after a data-integrity audit: 'Oregon's electoral system is one of the most secure, effective, and accessible in the nation' (OPB)

candidates.name: Christine Drazan
candidates.background: State senator since October 2025 and former Oregon House Republican leader (2019-2021); grew up in Klamath Falls and worked as a Capitol staffer before politics. The 2022 Republican nominee for governor, she lost to Kotek 46.9-43.5. Won the May 19 Republican primary with 41% over Ed Diehl and Chris Dudley, setting up a rematch.
priorities: Lower the cost of living by cutting taxes and regulations
Reduce homelessness with accountability, 'fewer needles and more cops'

cost.label: Blames government for the affordability crisis; would lower taxes, cut regulatory burdens, and reduce the cost of state services (campaign site)

housing.label: Targets regulatory barriers and forest management policies as the obstacles to homeownership; property tax relief for seniors (campaign site)

immigration.label: Says Oregon's sanctuary laws 'have gone too far,' citing releases of violent offenders; backs law enforcement cooperation across jurisdictions (KATU)

taxes.label: Cites a 77% rise in business taxes since 2019, repeats 'we have to lower taxes', and pledges to balance the budget without new taxes (KATU)

climate.label: As House GOP leader she joined 2020 quorum denials to block cap-and-trade climate legislation and demanded a referendum on it; 20% lifetime League of Conservation Voters score (Wikipedia)

education.label: Prioritizes parental authority in education and opposes 'radical ideologies' in schools (campaign site)

safety.label: 'Fewer needles and more cops to restore safe communities'; homelessness should be 'rare and temporary, not chronic' (campaign site)

repro.label: Endorsed by Oregon Right to Life in 2022; described as standing alone among that field in her anti-abortion views (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: 2022 platform pledged to 'ban ballot harvesting', create a 'permanent task force on election integrity', and direct the attorney general to investigate and prosecute voter fraud allegations (Ballotpedia)

health.label: Voted no on HB 2010, the 2025 provider-tax package securing Oregon Health Plan Medicaid funding, with the GOP objecting it raised taxes without a supermajority (Jefferson Public Radio)
